messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT ALERT — potential cross-tenant routing anomaly detected for Customer=AcmeCorp (VPC, dedicated pool dp-4721). Elevated 5xx and strange destination IPs in proxy logs. Pager fired.

pagerduty: Paging: on-call alicia (SRE) — please acknowledge. Incident severity P1.

alicia: ack — I'm on it. Pulling router/controller logs and proxy traces now.

alicia: quick snapshot: spike in 5xx started @ 1835001000, correlated with routing-controller deploy at 1834999800. Seeing route entries for tenant prefix 10.200.0.0/16 matching a shared route table.

alicia: log excerpt:
```
[1835001054] proxy: req_id=rx-9a2 tenant=acme path=/generate X-Forwarded-For=10.200.12.5 -> upstream=10.201.4.8 status=200
[1835001060] proxy: req_id=rx-9b3 tenant=acme path=/generate X-Forwarded-For=10.200.12.5 -> upstream=10.202.11.2 status=500
[1835001080] router: route-lookup src=10.200.12.0/24 matched route=shared-route-34 owner=global
```

marta: do we have any evidence responses for acme requests were served from other customers' containers/tenants? any PII exposure?

alicia: short answer: evidence of request routing to unexpected upstreams. Example header traces show X-Tenant: acme but connection landed on container with tenant-id=cn-19 (not acme). Sample trace (sanitized):
```
trace_id=tr-44a: client=10.200.12.5 header[X-Tenant]=acme -> backend=10.202.11.2 meta.tenant=cn-19
```
No clear writes to durable storage yet; most hits are in-memory inference requests. Still treating as potential cross-tenant exposure.

chao: recommended immediate mitigations: 1) isolate dp-4721 routing table from shared route set; 2) deploy ACLs to block cross-tenant east-west; 3) rollback routing-controller to previous stable. I can own step 1+2.

chao: applying ACL now (will patch and report):
```
# isolate pool dp-4721
rctl routes remove --pool dp-4721 --from shared-route-34
# explicit DROP for tenant prefix
iptables -I FORWARD -s 10.200.0.0/16 -d 10.0.0.0/8 -j DROP
```

ops-bot: change submitted: CL-8672 by chao -> route remove accepted, iptables rules applied to dp-4721 nodes (rolled to 5% -> 50% -> 100%).

alicia: confirmed on-proxy: connection table no longer shows cross-tenant matches for 10.200.*, beginning @ 1835001500. Running synthetic canary against AcmeCorp VPC now.

alicia: canary curl (sanitized):
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <acme-token>" https://proxy.redwood.internal/generate -d '{"prompt":"hello"}'
# response: 200 OK, meta.tenant=acme
```

marta: good. Customer impact: estimated 1.2% of Acme requests had misrouted responses between 18:30-18:40 UTC. No persisted writes observed. Need customer communication + offer deeper trace audit.

alicia: escalating to incident lead + timeline: root cause likely routing-controller bug that merged prefixes from shared route set into tenant route table on certain scale events. Verified with diff of route snapshots pre/post deploy.

chao: rolling back routing-controller to stable v2.9.1 now. Deploy bot: routing-controller rollback triggered (#rollback-1835001600).

ops-bot: rollback completed across clusters at 1835001723. Monitoring for error rate regressions.

alicia: metrics improving. 5xxs back to baseline by 1835001880. No new cross-tenant traces after ACL applied and rollback.

marta: summary for handoff to night oncall (lee_sre): 
- Customer: AcmeCorp (dp-4721) impacted by routing mismatch; ~1.2% requests misrouted; no persistent data writes found.
- Mitigations applied: route removal for dp-4721, iptables ACLs on nodes, routing-controller rollback.
- Next steps: full routing-controller audit, add route isolation unit test, customer-facing incident note draft (security-runbook review).

alicia: tagging @lee_sre for handoff. please verify retention of traces and coordinate with CSM for customer notification in AM.

lee_sre: handoff acknowledged. I'll own postmortem and coordinate external comms. Please drop repro steps + route snapshots into the incident ticket.

alicia: adding artifacts to INC-4721: route-diff, proxy-traces, iptables change logs, synthetic canary results. Action items: (1) postmortem, (2) add pre-deploy route invariant check in CI, (3) automate ACL scaffold for new dedicated pools.

marta: thanks all. marking incident as mitigated but keeping channel open for any late findings. (reacted :white_check_mark:)
